steps.text: Melt butter in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Stir in orzo and sauté until lightly browned.
Stir in chicken broth and bring to boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer until orzo is tender and liquid is absorbed, 15 to 20 minutes.
Mix in Parmesan cheese and 1/4 cup chopped basil. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer to a shallow bowl and garnish with remaining basil.

raw_recipe.headline: Orzo with Parmesan and Basil
raw_recipe.description: This Parmesan orzo is sautéed in butter, simmered in chicken stock, then mixed with Parmesan cheese and fresh basil for an easy, flavorful side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Orzo with Parmesan and Basil

review.reviewBody: This is one of the most perfect side dishes I have ever made. I do what the recipe states except I do not add any basil. While the orzo is cooking in the chicken broth I saute 8 oz of sliced mushrooms in olive oil, set aside in a bowl and then saute an entire bag, maybe 10 oz of baby spinach in olive oil for maybe 30 seconds and then when the orzo is done cooking I mix it altogether and add the parm cheese. I make this with any meat and it is always LOVED.

Very good recipe with marvelous flavor. I did note that I needed a 1/2 can more of chicken broth to finish cooking the orzo. Served with Roasted Chicken and a Orange, Walnut, Gorgonzola and Mixed Greens Salad with Fresh Citrus Vinaigrette from this site.

This is better than using a Rice a Roni box of something or another. You do want to make sure & use fresh basil. We grow some every summer so this is when I'll make this the most cause even store bought isn't always as good as right out of the garden. My big pet peeve is the "grated parmesan cheese". Very seldom do you find a recipe that states if it is fresh or a container of dry parmesan. We used fresh & then dry putting some dry stuff on some. Hands down hubby & I both liked the fresh. It is hard to mix into the cooked orzo because it melts so fast but still will use the fresh & maybe more of it.

This was wonderful. I did deviate from the recipe. I added two diced cloves of garlic to the butter before I added the orzo. I also added about 2 cups of frozen chopped spinach instead of basil when I added the broth. I found it necessary to add an additional half cup of broth to finish cooking the orzo. It got rave reviews. I will be making this again. It is a delicious side dish that is easy and quick to prepare.

Easy to make, I have a very low simmer on my gas stove, at 12 mins I still had a ton of liquid, had to raise the heat. When ready, stirred in the park an covered, turned off heat. Just before serving I tossed in the basil and zested a lemon... really brightened it up. Will make again, always have these ingredients on hand.

I make this often. I do use a combo of unsalted butter and olive oil to sauté the orzo; other than that I make the dish as is. Good with just about any main dish. I have stirred in shrimp and whatever steamed vegetables I have on hand for a main dish.

I put my own spin to this recipe. It’s similar to my risotto recipe. After I toasted the orzo, I added a little bit more butter and sautéed a sweet onion. Then I added the chicken broth There was still liquid in the pan as the orzo started to puff up then I added the mushrooms and green peas and the Parmesan cheese. Pecorino Romano works just as good if there’s no Parmesan. I added my Italian spices, some pepper, some thyme, and it came out amazing.
I added sliced mushrooms half way through the browning of the Orzo… it was absolutely delicious and paired well with my braised short ribs!

Everyone loved this. The orzo had enough broth because I covered it with a lid. Absolutely fabulous! I used grated Romano cheese (had on hand, and gives an extra punch). Had left over plum tomatoes so I sautéed them with olive oil, garlic, salt, pepper and added in after orzo cooked. It gave it extra fluid that the orzo needs when sitting. So glad I found this recipe!

This has been a favorite in my family since I started making it. I have to make a double or quadruple recipe every time and it still doesn't last long. 

I always use at least twice the basil. In fact, my wife and I decided to start an inside herb garden in order to have enough fresh basil to make this recipe often.

Recently I've been adding cubed, skillet seared chicken thighs just before I add the basil and cheese. It's fantastic.

One of the best things about this recipe is how it reheats in the microwave. It tastes and feels just like fresh cooked.

Great idea that I tweaked to my preference. Made this the first time to the recipe and felt that it needed a little more oomph for creaminess. I would add some milk, heavy cream, or yogurt just to make it a bit more creamy. The second time I made this, I was having a migraine so was avoiding cheese. I made a half portion and did everything but cheese. I also added garlic powder, ground thyme, and chopped tomatoes (removing the seeds). It was soooo good and went well with my sautéed chicken thighs. Next time I’ll add some onions while browning the orzo and I know that will take it to the next level.
This was great! Will definitely make it again. Could use a little more seasoning so I will add sautéed garlic and mushrooms after the orzo cooks and I think it will be perfect.
YUM
Good. I would use less parm and basil next time.
My go to recipe for a quick side dish! Love the nutty flavor and easy to follow.
I made as directed with one small modification: when I needed more liquid I used Chardonnay…because I cook with wine and sometimes add it to the food. Easy peasy and tasty.
Loved it and easy to make, we just added shallots and lemon zest
My family loved this recipe, I doubled it and added sauteed onions,

I love the idea and it was pretty good, but I think the next time I make this I need to do some things differently on my end. Less salt (I put a bit more than needed), cook it a little longer so it can be softer and then next time have the chicken broth (I forgot to get that and read that I could substitute it with salted butter in water, so I prepped that and added it later to the orzo as it cooked). I think next time it will be 5 stars. I had this with collard greens and seasoned, buttered salmon.
Used this recipe for years. I leave out the basil and just have orzo & cheese
